A Kaplan-Meier curve is the share of subjects still free of the event at each
time, dropping in steps as events occur. Drawn with `ax.step`, it is read as a
step chart: the probability at each time, and nothing else. What the figure is
read for is lost -- which times are censored (a subject who left the study
without the event, where the curve does *not* step), the confidence band, and
the median survival.

`maidr.plot_survival()` draws the curve from its numbers and reads it as a
survival curve: each censored time is announced as censored and can be reached
with the rotor, the band is announced after the estimate, and the description
(`d`) gives each arm's median survival, or says it was not reached.

`SURVIVAL` is **experimental** and may change without a deprecation period:
see [Plot Type Stability](../stability.qmd).

::: {.callout-warning title="Prototype"}
This is one of the experimental plot types. It has not been through a user
study, and it may change without a deprecation period. See
[Plot type stability](../stability.qmd).
:::

## Setup

```{python}
#| warning: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Just import maidr package: plt.show() now renders accessible output #<<
import maidr  #<<
```

## One arm

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Kaplan-Meier curve of overall survival over 18 months, with a shaded confidence band and a censoring tick at month 15

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import maidr  #<<

months = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18]
survival = [1.0, 0.88, 0.71, 0.5, 0.41, 0.34, 0.29]
lower = [0.88, 0.76, 0.59, 0.38, 0.29, 0.22, 0.17]
upper = [1.0, 1.0, 0.83, 0.62, 0.53, 0.46, 0.41]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
maidr.plot_survival(  #<<
    months, survival, lower=lower, upper=upper, censored=[15], ax=ax  #<<
)  #<<
ax.set_xlabel("Months")
ax.set_ylabel("Survival probability")
ax.set_title("Overall survival")

plt.show()  #<<
```

Left and Right move along the times. Each stop announces the survival
probability and the band around it, and month 15 is announced as censored.
The curve reaches one half at month 9, which the description gives as the
median survival.

## Comparing arms

Each call on the same axes adds an arm to one chart, so Up and Down switch
between arms at the same time. A censoring time that is not one of the times
given is added as a point of its own, at the survival in force then: the
Treatment arm holds at 0.79 through month 12, where a subject was censored.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Kaplan-Meier curves of a control and a treatment arm over 18 months, with censoring ticks

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import maidr  #<<

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
maidr.plot_survival(  #<<
    [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18],
    [1.0, 0.88, 0.71, 0.5, 0.41, 0.34, 0.29],
    censored=[15],
    label="Control",
    ax=ax,
)
maidr.plot_survival(  #<<
    [0, 3, 6, 9, 15],
    [1.0, 0.95, 0.86, 0.79, 0.72],
    censored=[12, 18],
    label="Treatment",
    ax=ax,
)
ax.set_xlabel("Months")
ax.set_ylabel("Survival probability")
ax.set_title("Overall survival by arm")
ax.legend(title="Arm")

plt.show()  #<<
```

The rotor offers the censored times as a unit of its own, so a reader can jump
from one to the next and hear how much of the tail is still backed by
subjects. Control reaches one half at month 9; Treatment never does, and the
description says its median was not reached.

## From lifelines

With [lifelines](https://lifelines.readthedocs.io/) installed, a fitted
`KaplanMeierFitter` is read the same way when you plot it: the estimate, its
confidence band and the times the fitter recorded as censored. Nothing in
maidr imports lifelines; the reading is wired up when your own code imports
it.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter
from lifelines.datasets import load_waltons

import maidr

df = load_waltons()
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for group, rows in df.groupby("group"):
    KaplanMeierFitter().fit(rows["T"], rows["E"], label=group).plot_survival_function(
        ax=ax, show_censors=True
    )

plt.show()
```
